sections.h2: Norfolk Highlands Home Prices and Market Pace
sections.html:
In the 24 months from November 15, 2024 to November 14, 2026, 178 residential sales closed in Norfolk Highlands (Chesapeake, VA) according to REIN MLS records. The median sold price was $344,750, close to the citywide median of $420,000, and homes took a median of 10 days to sell, faster than the citywide median of 18 days. These figures come from closed sales, which show what homes actually sold for rather than asking prices.

The middle half of Norfolk Highlands sales closed between $301,125 and $398,750, or about $219 per square foot against $219 citywide. Split by year, the median sold price in the most recent 12 months ($350,000, 108 sales) was about 7% higher than in the earlier 12 months ($328,000, 70 sales). The typical home sold right at its list price (median sale-to-list ratio of 100%).

Most recent Norfolk Highlands sales were in ZIP code 23325, with a meaningful share in 23320.

sections.h2: What Stands Out About Norfolk Highlands
sections.html: The median Norfolk Highlands home is about 1,510 square feet, smaller than the 1,970 square foot citywide median. 99% of sales here were detached homes, versus 76% citywide. 59% of Norfolk Highlands homes went under contract within 14 days of listing, compared with 44% of Chesapeake sales overall.

sections.h2: When Norfolk Highlands Homes Sell and How Far Prices Range
sections.html:
Closings in Norfolk Highlands were busiest in March (23 sales across the two years) and slowest in January (8 sales). Sold prices ran from $175,000 to $625,000, a spread of 3.6x between the lowest and highest sale. 82% of homes closed at or above list price and 2% closed at least 5% below it.

sections.h2: What Kinds of Homes Sell in Norfolk Highlands
sections.html:
99% of the sales were detached homes and 1% were attached homes (townhomes or condos). The median home was about 1,510 square feet, with the middle half of sales running from roughly 1,306 to 1,967 square feet. 56% of the homes that sold had 3 bedrooms.

Home ages vary widely here: about 80% of sales were built between 1950 and 2018, with a median year built of 1977.
